diagnostic_evidence.quote: By a similar reasoning, $\kappa=0$ is always an eigenvalue for any $n$, since we may choose $v\equiv w$ to be any harmonic function on $D$, again without imposing any boundary conditions.
noting that the set of harmonic functions on a non-empty $D$ has infinite dimension

issues.failure_explanation: The text first asserts that kappa=0 is an eigenvalue, with eigenspace {(h,h) : h harmonic}, which it notes is infinite dimensional, and then concludes that 0 lies in the continuous spectrum. Infinite dimensionality of an eigenspace places a spectral value in the point spectrum (of infinite multiplicity); it gives no information about the continuous spectrum. The inference is invalid and contradicts the preceding sentence that kappa=0 is an eigenvalue.

failure_location.quote: we conclude that $0$ belongs to the \emph{continuous spectrum} of the ITP \cite{Kubrusly2012}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'continuous spectrum' by 'point spectrum with infinite-dimensional eigenspace' (or delete the classification).
issues.overall_effect: The spectral classification of kappa=0 is wrong; no formal result depends on it, since the exclusion of kappa=0 is justified independently of the classification.
issues.title: Infinite-dimensional eigenspace at kappa=0 misclassified as continuous spectrum
issues.why_classification: A one-clause correction removes the false classification; every theorem, criterion, and the exclusion of kappa=0 survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This is in contradiction with the assumption that $\kappa^\star\ne 0\ne \int_Dn_p'\left|w_p\right|^2$, proving \cref{thm:bifurc}.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses give continuous differentiability only on the punctured interval, so v_p' and w_p' need not stay bounded as p tends to p-star and the claim that the integral factor stays bounded does not follow. Read literally the limit argument fails; read as a reductio assuming continuous differentiability at p-star it only yields that the trajectory is not C^1 there, weaker than the stated conclusion that it is non-differentiable. The statement itself is recoverable by assuming differentiability at p-star and evaluating the derived identity at p-star (forcing I(p-star) non-zero against I(p-star)=0), but that argument is not written.

failure_location.quote: Letting $p\to p^\star$, the right-hand side above goes to zero since $\textup{Im}\left(\kappa_{p^\star}^2\right)=0$ and because the integral factor stays bounded as a consequence of the continuous differentiability of the eigenfunction trajectory near $p^\star$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the last paragraph by the reductio: if the trajectory were differentiable at p-star, the differentiated identity would hold at p-star and give kappa' I(p-star) = (1/2) kappa int n'|w|^2 non-zero, contradicting I(p-star)=0 obtained from Lemma zeronorm and continuity; apply the same fix to the proof of cor:bifurc.
issues.overall_effect: As written the paper's main general bifurcation theorem and its corollary are unproved, so the advertised generalization of the disk theory to arbitrary domains and inhomogeneous media rests on an unestablished input.
issues.title: Limit step in the proof of the general bifurcation theorem is unsupported by its hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The conclusion survives, but only after replacing the final inference by a different (contained) argument, which exceeds a routine local edit while requiring no new global architecture or loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes the undivided identity kappa kappa' I = (1/2) kappa^2 int n'|w|^2; the displayed formula divides by I(p). The hypotheses (C^1 at p, real kappa) do not exclude I(p)=0, and such points are exactly the ones studied elsewhere (cor:bifurc assumes I(p-star)=0). At any such point where the trajectory is C^1 the numerator also vanishes by the same identity, so the asserted formula degenerates to 0/0 and is undefined.

with $\overline I$ taking only non-positive values

Therein, we observe that the indicator becomes positive if and only if an eigenvalue trajectory is (i) real and (ii) traveling to the right.
Theory confirms this, since \cref{cor:bifurc} relates the sign of $\overline{I}$ to the sign of the derivative of a real trajectory.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition divides I by (a_m pi/2)(1-p^2), so with the disk formula proved in the appendix one gets I-bar = |alpha|^2 J_m(kappa)^2 >= 0 on real disk trajectories and sign(I-bar) = -sign(I) whenever p>1. Lemma bifurc_ord gives kappa' = kappa int n'|w|^2 /(2I), hence for kappa>0 and p>0 sign(kappa')=sign(I)=-sign(I-bar) when p>1. Every subsequent sign statement asserts the opposite (disk indicator strictly negative / uniformly non-positive, fitted laws I-bar ~ -|p-p^star|^alpha, and I-bar positive exactly for rightward-moving real branches), and the claimed sign relation is moreover attributed to cor:bifurc, which contains no sign relation at all. The two sign conventions cannot both be correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the convention consistent: either replace 2/(a_m pi (1-p^2)) in eq:ind_simpl by 2/(a_m pi (p^2-1)) and flip the sign in prop:annulus:bifurc_ord, or reverse every sign claim about I-bar in the numerical sections and cite lem:bifurc_ord instead of cor:bifurc.
issues.overall_effect: The sign interpretation of the indicator in all numerical sections and the sign in the identity of prop:annulus:bifurc_ord cannot both stand; the 'theory confirms this' sign claim is sign-inverted and mis-cited. Zero sets and bifurcation criteria are unaffected.
issues.title: Sign inconsistency in the normalized indicator
issues.why_classification: A sign flip in one normalization and its derived formula (or in the prose sign statements) restores full consistency; the vanishing locus, all bifurcation criteria, and every theorem survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: An immediate consequence is that, by \cref{cor:bifurc_sufficient}, a real (piecewise-smooth) eigenvalue trajectory undergoes bifurcation if and only if $\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_1)}=r\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_r)}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing v_p(rho,theta)=f_p(rho) phi(m theta) gives ||v_p||_{L^infty(dB_rho)}=|f_p(rho)| and, with normalized angular measure, ||v_p||_{L^2(dB_rho)}=sqrt(a_m pi)|f_p(rho)| (with arclength measure an extra sqrt(rho) appears). Hence ||v||_{L^infty(dB_1)}=r||v||_{L^infty(dB_r)} is equivalent to ||v||_{L^2(dB_1)}=r||v||_{L^2(dB_r)}, or to ||v||_{L^2(dB_1)}=sqrt(r)||v||_{L^2(dB_r)} with arclength measure, but never to equality of the two L2 norms as stated; the claimed equivalence fails for every r different from 1.

failure_location.quote: By the assumed polar-coordinate separability in \cref{eq:annulus:functions}, this is actually equivalent to $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing factor r (or sqrt(r) with arclength measure) in the stated L2 equality.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised L2-norm characterization of annulus bifurcation points is false; the L-infinity criterion and all theorems remain valid.
issues.title: Missing factor r in the claimed L2 reformulation of the annulus bifurcation criterion
issues.why_classification: A one-factor correction yields a true equivalent form of a criterion whose correct L-infinity version is already stated and proved; nothing else changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We observe eight quadratic bifurcations that turn pairs of complex-conjugate eigenvalues into pairs of real eigenvalues and vice versa.
in \cref{fig:annulus:fit} we can observe an empirical scaling halfway between $-|p-p^\star|^{1/2}$ and $-|p-p^\star|^{2/3}$
suggesting that any such root of $\overline{I}$ must be of order $1/2$, by \cref{cor:bifurc_sufficient}
then $p\mapsto\kappa_p$ displays a bifurcation of order $M$ at $p^\star$
The table displays the rate $\alpha$ such that $\overline{I}(p)\sim-|p-p^\star|^\alpha$, estimated based on the data.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem cor:bifurc_sufficient forces the indicator of a real branch to vanish at a bifurcation of order M with exponent exactly 1-1/M, and its converse recovers M from that exponent; rem:annulus:ord accordingly states that the observed order-2 roots must be of order 1/2. The eight events are explicitly classified as quadratic bifurcations, yet their fitted exponents are reported to lie strictly between 1/2 and 2/3 and are read as evidence that the bifurcations are close to cubic. No algebraic bifurcation of integer order yields such an exponent, and cubic order is in any case excluded by the described branch pattern (two real branches on one side and a conjugate pair on the other is the even-M pattern of rem:angle, whereas M=3 requires exactly one real branch on each side).

failure_location.quote: This intermediate scaling suggests that the bifurcations are close to being cubic rather than quadratic.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-examine the exponent fits and the event classification and withdraw the 'intermediate / near-cubic' reading: if the eight events are quadratic bifurcations the fitted exponents must be 1/2, and if the fits are reliable the events are not integer-order algebraic bifurcations and must not be described as quadratic or near-cubic.
issues.overall_effect: The classification of the eight events as quadratic bifurcations and the claim that the numerics confirm cor:bifurc_sufficient cannot both stand; the r-to-0 'cubic limit' interpretation built on the intermediate scaling is unsupported.
issues.title: Reported indicator exponents contradict the claimed bifurcation orders and Theorem cor:bifurc_sufficient
issues.why_classification: Resolution requires re-analysing the numerical data and revising the interpretation (including the r-to-0 cubic-limit narrative) or the bifurcation classification; no theorem must be rebuilt, but a claimed confirmation of the theory has to be withdrawn or re-established, which is more than a local edit.
